entities.summary: István Várday was a Hungarian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal, born into a noble family in the late 15th century. He rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church, becoming a prominent figure in the Eastern European clergy during the tumultuous reign of King Matthias Corvinus. Várdai's influence extended beyond his immediate circle, as he played a key role in shaping the Church's response to the Ottoman Empire's expansion into Eastern Europe. He was a strong advocate for the rights of the Hungarian people and worked tirelessly to promote their interests at the highest levels of the Church. Várdai's legacy can be seen in the many institutions and organizations he helped establish, including the Diocese of Eger, which continues to serve the people of Hungary to this day. The cardinal's impact on Hungarian history is still felt today, with many regarding him as a champion of national pride and religious freedom. As a prominent figure in the Church, Várdai's actions had far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of Eastern European history and leaving an indelible mark on the region's cultural and religious landscape.

entities.summary:
István Várday was a Hungarian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a crucial role in the Counter-Reformation during the 15th century. Born in Szabolcs County, Hungary in 1420, Várdai rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church, becoming Bishop of Győr in 1458 and eventually Cardinal-Deacon of Santa Maria in Minerva in 1462.

 He was instrumental in the establishment of several monasteries and colleges, including the famous Esterházy College in Sopron, which became a center for humanist education. Várdai also contributed significantly to the translation of Latin texts into Hungarian, helping to preserve ancient knowledge during a time of significant cultural upheaval.

 Despite facing opposition from Protestant reformers, Várdai remained steadfast in his devotion to the Catholic Church, and his legacy as a champion of orthodoxy has endured for centuries. His contributions to education, literature, and the spread of Catholicism helped shape the intellectual and religious landscape of medieval Europe.
